title: Stuffed shells, cheese- and spinach-filled, no sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed shells are large pasta shells filled with a mixture of cheese and spinach. They are sold without sauce, making them convenient for quick snacks or adding to salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally these shells are baked in Italian cuisine, often under a tomato sauce.
The combination of cheese (usually ricotta or mozzarella) and spinach provides a pleasant balance of flavor and texture.
Without sauce the product is easier to store and transport, requiring no additional reheating.
Spinach retains most of its vitamins when the product is flash‑frozen after preparation.
In some countries the shells are used as a base for vegetarian meals.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The cheese in the filling supplies high‑quality animal protein important for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese and spinach contain B2, B6 and folate, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese provides calcium, which contributes to bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Spinach is high in lutein and vitamin C, helping combat free radicals.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Spinach adds fiber that aids normal digestion.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dairy proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared stuffed shells can contain added salt, which should be considered on low‑sodium diets.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of cheese and pasta, the dish is relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Shells can be eaten cold in a salad, reheated in a microwave or oven, added to soups, or used as part of sandwich spreads. They pair well with olive oil, fresh herbs, or a light yogurt dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in its original packaging in the refrigerator at 0 °C‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. For freezing, place in an airtight bag and store up to 2 months. Discard if any off‑odor or mold appears.
